stimuli.title: Sana, Isha, Hema, Pia, Deepa, Farah, Esha, Aditi occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Isha occupies floor 1, flat B.
• Farah lives above Esha.
• Pia and Esha live in the same flat letters.
• Pia lives below Esha.
• Isha and Esha live in the same flat letters.
• Isha and Aditi live in the same flat letters.
• Sana lives below Pia.
• Hema lives above Deepa.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some files are lockers. All lockers are cheques. No cheques is a notes.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are cheques.
II. Some lockers are notes.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are lockers. Some lockers are cheques. All cheques are notes.
Conclusions:
I. All files are notes.
II. No lockers is a notes.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No files is a lockers. Some lockers are cheques. All cheques are notes.
Conclusions:
I. All files are notes.
II. Some notes are lockers.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are lockers. All lockers are cheques. No cheques is a notes.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are not lockers.
II. No lockers is a notes.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: T < R > Q < X < U.
Conclusions: I. U ≥ Q   II. Q ≤ T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural savings secure = re vo lu
rural credit digital = mi ni lu
savings credit banking = re mi su
secure digital banking = su ni vo
rural savings banking = re lu su
What is the code for “rural”?
questions.explanation: Answer: lu. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = lu, savings = re, secure = vo, credit = mi, digital = ni, banking = su.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 68 km east, turns left and walks 60 km, then turns left and walks 23 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 75. Net displacement is 45 km east and 60 km north. By Pythagoras, √(45² + 60²) = 75 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 21 km east, turns left and walks 8 km, then turns left and walks 15 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: C is the mother of B. H is the son of B. E is the father of B. How is H related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. E is a parent of B, and H is B’s son. Hence H is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of H. H is the mother of E. D is the father of A and H. How is A related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of E’s mother H. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A is the only daughter of F. F is the father of A. H is the son of A. B is the sister of F. How is F related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of A, and A is H’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 41 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 29. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 41 − 13 + 1 = 29.

questions.stem: In a queue of 51 candidates, a candidate is 9th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. New front rank = 9+4 = 13. Back rank = 51 − 13 + 1 = 39.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1600. It is marked above cost and sold at a 25% discount on marked price, earning 12% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2389.33. Selling price = 1600 × 112/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.75 = 2389.33.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 26 days and B in 39 days. They work together for 3 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need?
questions.explanation: Answer: 21. Use 78 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 78 − 3×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 192 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 14 km/h and stream speed is 2 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹21000 for 12 months. B invests ₹42000 for 4 months. Total profit is ₹50000. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 20000. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 8. B’s share = total × 8/(20) = 20000.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹16000 at 15% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Answer: 360. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 16000 × (15/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 90 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 18. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 18.

questions.stem: The average of 32 numbers is 54. One number, 66, is replaced and the average rises by 5. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 226. Total increases by 32 × 5. New number = 66 + 160.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 7 years, their combined age will be 90 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 57. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 14 = 90; x = 19, so father = 57.

questions.stem: A train of length 120 m crosses a 120 m platform at 82.8 km/h. Find crossing time in seconds (to two decimals).
A village has 4400 registered customers. This increases by 25% in year 1 and decreases by 20% in year 2. What is the final number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 4400. Apply successive factors: 4400 × 125/100 × 80/100.
